description:
Demolition of existing
buildings and construction of a building rising from two to four storeys including a basement, with roof terraces at second and third floors, roof-top PV Panels and amenity balconies to the front and side elevations to facilitate provision of a mixed use development comprising seven residential units (3 x 1-bed,
2 x 2-bed and 2 x 3-bed) (Use Class C3) and commercial unit at ground
and basement floors (Use Class E), with associated refuse/recycle and bicycle storage.

decision_conditions:
The intensive use of the external communal terrace
in close proximity to No. 1 Davies Lane and No. 560 High Road Leytonstone would
have a detrimental impact upon the amenity of adjoining occupiers as 6 flats
would have access to this shared. The increased activity, general noise and
disturbance would be unacceptable contrary to Policy 57 (Amenity) of the
adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

The proposed building by reason of its depth and
height would have a detrimental impact on the residential amenity of the
occupiers at No. 560 High Road Leytonstone that would result in a serious loss
of outlook and light, creating an increased sense of enclosure, contrary to
Policy 57 (Amenity) of the adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

The application as submitted relates to the
demolition and construction of a mixed use building with commercial space at
lower and ground floor levels. Therefore, one of the prerequisites is that the
proposed commercial use must be assessed whether it is appropriate within the
existing street frontage. Also, the compatibility of the proposed use(s) with
existing, proposed and adjoining uses are also a material consideration. The
proposed use has been stated as falling  within Use Class E which is not
sufficient. Use Class E contains a myriad of uses, depending on the proposed
use within Use Class E further consideration alongside residential may be required.
Therefore, the principle of development in relation to Policy 7 (Encouraging
mixed use development) of the adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024) could not be
established.

Notwithstanding the first point of refusal, an
assessment with regard to the design of the building could not be made as the
proposed use of the lower and ground floor commercial space was not provided.
Therefore, compliance with the aims and objectives of Policy 53 (Delivering
High Quality Design) of the adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024) could not be
assessed.

The proposed development provides a poor standard
of accommodation for future occupiers in relation to insufficient internal
storage across all flats, insufficient gross internal floor area of second
floor flat 5 and the unacceptable provision of two single aspect north facing
dwellings (First floor flat 3 and second floor flat 5). Therefore, the proposal
would be contrary to Policy 56 (Residential Space Standards) of the adopted
Local Plan Part 1 (2024), Policy D6 of The London Plan (2021) and London Plan
Guidance – Housing Design Standards (June 2023).

Due to insufficient screening and close proximity
to No. 1 Davies Lane, the proposed external terraces are unacceptable. The
terraces would provide direct overlooking into No. 1 Davies Lane to the
detriment and well-being of the occupiers contrary to Policy 57 (Amenity) of
the adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

Due to insufficient information pertaining to the
ongoing maintenance in relation to the street trees along the northern
elevation (Davies Lane), an assessment could not be made. As the trees mature
and their crowns grow larger, the resultant juxtaposition is likely to lead to
problems, particularly as this elevation includes balconies and widows serving
the properties. The increased requirement for arboricultural works has not been
taken into consideration contrary to the aims an objectives of Policy 80
(Trees) of the adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

In the absence of a satisfactory Outline
Construction Logistic Plan, a full assessment of how the proposed development
would be built or serviced without severely affecting the public highway could
not be made in line with Policies T7 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy 65
(Construction Logistics Plans) of the adopted Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

The applicant failed to enter into a s106 agreement
and therefore not in compliance with Policy 94 (Infrastructure and Developer
Contributions) of the Emerging Local Pan (figures applicable at the time of the
assessment of the application):Car Free Development - the development is to be classified
as car-free and residents will not be eligible for parking permits.A condition survey of the carriageway and footways
fronting the site prior to the commencement of any works Financial contribution of £4,389.00 towards
the Epping Forest SAMM S106 contribution of £750 is requested toward
CLP monitoring.







S278 agreement to, Works will include but are not
limited to:Renewal of the footway on both frontages of the
site on High Road Leytonstone and Davies LaneRemoval of the redundant crossover on Davies LaneRemoval of the existing double yellow line on
Davies and extension of the CPZ parking bays including a traffic management
orderInstallation of a dropped kerb within 15 metres of
the bin store to facilitate bin collection







Financial contribution of 5% for s106 monitoring
fees.
